author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell revisits the official Covid nineteen timeline starting from January 2020, when the first cases in Wuhan were reported, and can't help but laugh at his own reaction back then. He admits he had no idea where Wuhan even was and joked he wouldn't start caring until the outbreak reached a part of China he'd actually heard of. It's a candid, self-deprecating look back at how casually the whole thing was dismissed in its earliest days, before anyone understood what was coming.

author: Russell Brand
description:
A stunning admission about how willingly Americans handed over their freedom during Covid, and what it revealed about our blind trust in institutions. The guest breaks down the strange psychology behind it: the same pharmaceutical companies tied to the opioid crisis and the Johnson and Johnson baby powder scandal suddenly became untouchable heroes, with people literally tattooing Pfizer onto their bodies. It also uncovered something deeper, when parents were forced to watch their kids' lessons at home, many saw for the first time exactly what the education system was teaching. A rare moment of clarity most people never got to see.

author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell takes on the digital ID rollout with a sharp satirical bit, playing a royal figure who can't stop congratulating himself on how "modern" the whole thing is while everyone else gets chipped and tracked. It's a biting jab at the disconnect between the people announcing these policies and the people who actually have to live under them. The absurdity of the framing makes the real point land even harder, digital ID was supposedly scrapped, and now it's quietly back.

author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell breaks down the game that's shaped how he moves through life, walking in a straight line no matter what's in the way, even if that means climbing over walls. When he introduced it to Laura, it led to one unforgettable night sneaking through the Chelsea Flower Show in the dark, while she insisted the whole time that they shouldn't be doing this. A small story that says a lot about the tension between his instinct to push forward and her instinct to protect.
